rubrics.justification: The response overcalls image quality and describes features not clearly visible in this image, especially a distinct compact ICM, cohesive TE, and clear full expansion/thinning zona. The embryo appears somewhat collapsed/poorly visualized rather than a textbook 3AA on the image alone.
It thoroughly integrates age, PCOS/high AMH, ovarian response, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrium, smoking, and prior ectopic history with prognosis and transfer considerations.

The reasoning is generally logical and structured, with a clear link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat confident quantitative adjustments and reliance on morphology despite limited image clarity.

Much of the advice is guideline-consistent (SET, antagonist suitability for PCOS, early scan after prior ectopic), but several recommendations are weakly supported or not routine guideline-based, including aspirin, ERA after one failure, immunologic workup/NK testing, endometrial scratching, and strong endorsement of PGT-A at age 32.

The response gives clear practical next steps for transfer, luteal support, early hCG/ultrasound follow-up, smoking cessation, and future evaluation. It loses some points because a few suggested interventions are not standard or may be overly prescriptive.
